newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - July 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - July 7.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- APPLE DAILY -- Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa appointed his personal driver as a civil servant without going through proper procedures. Former legislator Emily Lau said that by insisting on using his personal driver instead of government drivers, Tung has shown he does not trust civil servants.
-- Beijing said it does not intend to further increase the number of People's Liberation Army soldiers in Hong Kong, and might consider reducing it gradually.

-- EXPRESS NEWS -- Beijing's Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office has taken over the power to approve Chinese officials entering Hong Kong from Xinhua News Agency, but the Hong Kong Immigration Department said it still has the right to reject Chinese officials if necessary.
-- HONG KONG DAILY -- Several groups will hold demonstrations outside the Japanese consulate to mark the 60th anniversary of the Japanese invasion of China.
-- WEN WEI PO -- The Chinese economy continued to develop in a good direction. The Central Plannery Commission said adjusting price increases would not have a negative impact on the economy.

-- Over 80 per cent of residents of Beijing, Shanghai and Guangzhou were content with their living standard, and believed that it would not drop in the next five years. In general, better educated people were happier with life.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Police officers had not been told how to handle PLA deserters, absentees or law breakers, provoking fears of confusion over the execution of duties.
-- The head of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority was among the world's highest paid central bankers, as shown in a survey of their perks and pay.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Executive Councillor Tam Yiu-chung believed that the elderly should be given the option of euthanasia, or mercy killing.
